ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the picture, four identical standard dice are put together to form a 2×2 solid block. The front face of the front-left die has 1 written on it, and the front face of the front-right die has 2 written on it; the right face of the front-right die has 3 written on it, and the top face has 6 written on it; the right face of the farthest-right rear die has 4 written on it; the face above the rear-left die is marked with a question mark. Then reason: Take the front-right die as a reference. From the figure, it can be seen that its front face is 2, its right face is 3, and its top face is 6. For a standard die, the sums of opposite numbers are 7, so its left face is 4, its back face is 5, and its bottom face is 1. Because the numbers on the faces where adjacent dice touch are the same, the front-right die touches the front-left die on its left, so the right face of the front-left die is 4; the front face of the front-left die is known to be 1, so its back face is 6. The back of the front-right die touches the rear-right die, so the front face of the rear-right die is 5; and in the figure the right face of the rear-right die is 4, therefore its left face is 3. The rear-left die touches both the front-left die and the rear-right die: its front face equals the back face of the front-left die, which is 6; its right face equals the left face of the rear-right die, which is 3. Thus the rear-left die is known to have front face 6 and right face 3. For the same standard die, this orientation corresponds to a top face of 5, so 5 is written at the question mark.

method.method_draft: Use the front-right die as the orientation reference, then propagate contact faces. From the image, identify four dice in a 2-by-2 block: front-left shows front 1; front-right shows front 2, top 6, right 3; back-right shows right 4; the question mark is on the top of the back-left die. From the text, touching faces must have equal numbers and opposite faces sum to 7. On the front-right die, since right is 3, left is 4, so the front-left die has right face 4. Since front-right front is 2, its back is 5, so the back-right die has front face 5. Using identical dice with the same orientation pattern as the reference die, determine hidden faces: the back-right die with front 5 and right 4 has left face 3, so the back-left die has right face 3. Also the front-left die with front 1 and right 4 has back face 6, so the back-left die has front face 6. Finally, for an identical die with front 6 and right 3, the top face is 5. Therefore the question mark is 5.

Rory uses four identical standard dice to build the solid shown in the diagram.
Whenever two dice touch, the numbers on the touching faces are the same. The numbers on some of the faces of the solid are shown. What number is written on the face marked with question mark?
(On a standard die, the numbers on opposite faces add to 7.)
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Rory uses four identical standard dice to build the solid shown in the diagram. Whenever two dice touch, the numbers on the touching faces are the same. The numbers on some of the faces of the solid are shown. What number is written on the face marked with question mark? (On a standard die, the numbers on opposite faces add to 7.)
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the image, four identical standard dice are put together into a 2×2 three-dimensional block. The front face of the left-front die has 1 written on it, and the front face of the right-front die has 2 written on it; the right face of the right-front die has 3 written on it, and the top face has 6 written on it; the right face of the rightmost rear die has 4 written on it; the face above the left-rear die is marked with a question mark.
Then reason: Take the right-front die as the reference. From the image it can be seen that its front face is 2, its right face is 3, and its top face is 6. For a standard die, the numbers on opposite faces sum to 7, so its left face is 4, its back face is 5, and its bottom face is 1.
Because the numbers on the contacting faces of adjacent dice are the same, the right-front die contacts the left-front die on its left side, so the right face of the left-front die is 4; the front face of the left-front die is already known to be 1, so its back face is 6.
The back face of the right-front die contacts the right-rear die, so the front face of the right-rear die is 5; and in the image the right face of the right-rear die is 4, therefore its left face is 3.
The left-rear die simultaneously contacts the left-front die and the right-rear die: its front face equals the back face of the left-front die, which is 6; its right face equals the left face of the right-rear die, which is 3.
Thus the left-rear die is known to have front face 6 and right face 3. For the same standard die, this orientation corresponds to a top face of 5, so 5 is written at the question mark.
